newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama prepares for airport sell-off at end '97.
newsitem.headline: Panama prepares for airport sell-off at end '97.

text.p: Panama is set to start the privatization of its airports in December as part of wider plans to convert Panama into Central America's air cargo hub, the civil aviation authority (DAC) said Monday.

The DAC said the first phase of the government's airport privatization drive will be to sell the administrative and commercial parts of Panama City's international airport at Tocumen. The bid price is due to be set by the end of August or early September for auction in December, the DAC said.
Panama will be "the cargo distribution center for Central America, with most cargo coming from Asia and the United States," DAC spokesman Victor de la Hoz told Reuters.

The successful bidder for the airport -- which has yearly revenues of $25 million on one million passengers -- will also pick up the France Field airport in the province of Colon, 50 miles (80 km) from the capital.
Hoz said Colon's airport would be turned into a cargo hub and that the cargo service at Tocumen airport would be modernized to cope with increased demand.
"We have already had foreign companies from the U.S., Canada and Britain coming to visit the airport (Tocumen), interested in the privatization plans," Hoz added.
"What we are not going to privatize (in the first phase) are the control tower, air safety, and airport security. That will be managed by the civil aviation authority," he added.
The government is still studying what to include in its second airport privatization phase, Hoz said, with details to be announced by the end of August or early September.
((-- Paul de Bendern, Panama City newsroom 507 223 7739))
